description:
FILED s497b from the #2103 fatals battery (row "local on lexical-free special").  perl 5.40.3: `local $/ = \0` dies "Setting $/ to a reference to zero is forbidden", `\-1` "... to a negative integer is forbidden", a ref to a non-number likewise.  PCL stores it and get-input-record-separator reads a non-positive record length as slurp.
NOT SHIPPED in s497b because the die must happen at the ASSIGNMENT (the USER bar: fail in the same place); dying at the next readline is a different place, and turning |$/| into a magic box would put a setter on every `local $/` (the commonest slurp idiom) -- measure first.
REPRODUCER: eval { local $/ = \0; 1 } or print "died\n";   perl: died.  PCL: nothing.  Pl/t/fatals-01.t carries it as a TODO naming this task.
subject: `local $/ = \0` (and `$/ = \-1`, `\"abc"`) is ACCEPTED where perl dies `Setting $/ to a reference to zero is forbidden` -- $/ is a plain box with no store hook
